caption:
Instagram already told you what it measures. Watch time, likes per reach, and sends per reach — named publicly by Adam Mosseri, Instagram's head, and restated through 2026.

Notice what is not on that list. Follower count. Hashtag count. Posting at 7pm. Comment pods.

And notice the two words doing the work: per reach. Not likes. Likes divided by how many people saw it. A post with 40 likes from 300 people beats a post with 200 likes from 20,000, and the second one is the one people screenshot.

If you are starting out, this is the best news you will get all week: you do not need a big account. You need a high rate. Small accounts reach a bigger share of their own audience than large ones do.

Open your last 10 posts. Write down reach and sends for each. Divide. That column is your real scoreboard.
